symbols.name: d_n
symbols.def: Degree of the stage-\(n\) interference graph.

symbols.name: \ell
symbols.def: Generic positive seed-draw index, later restricted to \(\{1,\ldots,k_n\}\).

symbols.name: G_n
symbols.def: Uniformly drawn labeled simple \(d_n\)-regular graph on \(V_n\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: Realization of \(G_n\), revealed before the design is chosen.

symbols.name: \mathcal M_n(G)
symbols.def: Class of schedules satisfying ANI on \(G\) and the two endpoint empirical second-moment bounds, as constructed in Definition 1.

symbols.name: \mathcal D_G
symbols.def: Any graph-measurable probability law on assignments, chosen after observing \(G\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau
symbols.def: Measurable estimator based only on \((Z,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\) and the revealed graph \(G\).

symbols.name: A_G
symbols.def: Adjacency matrix of the revealed simple graph \(G\).

symbols.name: J_\ell
symbols.def: Independent uniform vertex draw for each \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,k_n\}\).

symbols.name: \pi_i(G)
symbols.def: On the branch \(M_n<n\), the positive probability \(\pi_i(G)=q_i(G)^{k_n}\) that unit \(i\) is fully control-exposed under the seed design.

symbols.name: w_i(z;G)
symbols.def: On the branch \(M_n<n\), the conditional weight \(w_i(z;G)=\mathbb E[k_n^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{k_n}\mathbf 1\{J_\ell=i\}\mid Z^{\mathrm{seed}}=z,G]\) for assignments of positive seed-design probability.

symbols.name: Q_G
symbols.def: On the branch \(M_n<n\), the matrix with \(Q_{G,ij}=\Pr(i,j\in C_G(Z^{\mathrm{seed}})\mid G)/[\pi_i(G)\pi_j(G)]-1\).

symbols.name: U(G,k_n)
symbols.def: Certificate \(U(G,k_n)=2/k_n+2\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2[(1-M_n/n)^{-k_n}-1]/[nM_n(1-M_n/n)]\) when \(M_n<n\), with the universal fallback value \(1\) otherwise.

symbols.name: \overline U(G)
symbols.def: Selected certificate \(\overline U(G)=\min\{1,U(G,k_n)\}\) when \(M_n<n\), and \(\overline U(G)=1\) when \(M_n\ge n\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}
symbols.def: Estimator returned by the finite compiler: when \(M_n<n\) and \(U(G,k_n)\le1\), use \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\); when \(M_n<n\) and \(U(G,k_n)>1\), or when \(M_n\ge n\), assign all units treatment and report the observed treated mean.

symbols.name: \mathsf H_B
symbols.def: Named proof handle that centers duplicate length-two-walk corrections and controls their trace moments by degree-preserving switchings.

assumptions.condition: The degree sequence satisfies \(d_n\ge3\) for every \(n\).
Conditional on \((n,d_n)\), \(G_n\) is uniform on the labeled simple \(d_n\)-regular graphs on \(V_n\).
For every \(i\in V_n\) and \(z,z'\in\{0,1\}^{V_n}\), equality \(z_j=z'_j\) for every \(j\in N_G[i]\) implies \(y_i(z)=y_i(z')\).
The treated endpoint vector satisfies \(n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}a_i^2\le1\).
The control endpoint vector satisfies \(n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}b_i^2\le1\).

definitions.name: Endpoint-\(L_2\) ANI class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n(G)=\{y:(\forall i,z,z')[(\forall j\in N_G[i],\ z_j=z'_j)\Rightarrow y_i(z)=y_i(z')],\ n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}a_i^2\le1,\ n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}b_i^2\le1\}\) at every stage \(n\).

definitions.name: Graph-conditioned unrestricted minimax risk
definitions.construction: \(R(G)=\inf_{\mathcal D_G\in\Delta(\{0,1\}^{V_n}),\,\widehat\tau}\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_n(G)}\mathbb E_{Z\sim\mathcal D_G,y}[(\widehat\tau(Z,Y^{\mathrm{obs}};G)-\tau_n)^2]\), where the estimator is measurable in only the displayed observed data and \(G\).

definitions.name: With-replacement neighborhood-seed design
definitions.construction: Draw \(J_1,\ldots,J_{k_n}\) independently and uniformly from \(V_n\), then assign \(Z^{\mathrm{seed}}_v=\mathbf 1\{v\in\bigcup_{\ell=1}^{k_n}N_G[J_\ell]\}\).

definitions.name: Observed-data Rao--Blackwell seed estimator
definitions.construction: On the branch \(M_n<n\), first set \(\pi_i(G)=q_i(G)^{k_n}>0\). For every assignment \(z\) of positive seed-design probability, compute \(w_i(z;G)=\mathbb E[k_n^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{k_n}\mathbf 1\{J_\ell=i\}\mid Z^{\mathrm{seed}}=z,G]\), and set \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}=\sum_{i\in V_n}w_i(Z^{\mathrm{seed}};G)y_i(Z^{\mathrm{seed}})-n^{-1}\sum_{i\in C_G(Z^{\mathrm{seed}})}y_i(Z^{\mathrm{seed}})/\pi_i(G)\). No object in this definition is formed on the branch \(M_n\ge n\).

definitions.name: Exact Schur covariance and deterministic risk certificate
Centered Boolean collision handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathsf H_B\) to write the difference between \(A_G^2+A_G-(d_n-1)I_n\) and \(B_2(G)\) as centered triangle and repeated-codegree graph matrices, decompose these matrices by graph shape, and apply degree-preserving switching trace moments separately below and above a polylogarithmic degree threshold.

definitions.name: Selected certified one-shot procedure
definitions.construction: First compare \(M_n\) with \(n\). If \(M_n\ge n\), do not form \(\pi_i(G)\), \(Q_G\), \(w_i(z;G)\), or \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\); assign \(Z=\mathbf 1_n\), report \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}y_i(\mathbf 1_n)\), and set \(\overline U(G)=1\). If \(M_n<n\), form the seed objects and \(U(G,k_n)\); use \(Z^{\mathrm{seed}}\), report \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}=\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\), and set \(\overline U(G)=U(G,k_n)\) when \(U(G,k_n)\le1\), while returning the same all-treated fallback and \(\overline U(G)=1\) when \(U(G,k_n)>1\).

statements.statement: For every finite revealed graph \(G\), the unrestricted design-and-estimator risk satisfies \[R(G)\ge\frac{1}{12\{\beta(G)+2\}}.\] The inequality holds against every graph-dependent assignment law and every measurable estimator because a pair of independent uniform-Beta Bernoulli endpoint schedules leaves posterior variance at least the displayed amount in the less observed arm.
statements.justification: This converts balanced two-arm observability, rather than a one-sided independent set, into an all-procedure finite-population minimax converse.
statements.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Theorem 3.2, lower-bounds risk through an induced independence number; it does not enforce comparable information about both signs of the GATE contrast.
statements.consumer: The random-regular packing theorem turns this finite-graph inequality into the rate lower bound required to certify any prospective full-policy experiment.

statements.statement: There is a universal constant \(C_\beta<\infty\) such that every admissible sequence satisfies \[\Pr\!\left\{\beta(G_n)\le C_\beta\frac{n\log(d_n+1)}{d_n^2}\right\}\longrightarrow1.\] The proof must be uniform over sequences that cross the sparse and coupling regimes. Below a sufficiently large universal multiple of \(\log n\), a degree-preserving switching enumeration directly under the uniform simple regular law must give the required \(o(1)\) failure probability, without conditioning a configuration model on simplicity. At and above that threshold, a contained binomial graph from the Kim--Vu sandwich transfers the decreasing balanced-hole event.
statements.justification: This theorem identifies the logarithmic balanced-hole scale by a uniform-simple switching argument below the verified sandwich threshold and monotone coupling above it.
statements.gap: CooperEtAl2002RandomRegular characterizes ordinary one-color independence, whereas this signed closed-neighborhood packing excludes only opposite-arm centers at graph distance at most two.
statements.consumer: Combined with Proposition 1, it rules out every design-estimator pair below order \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\).

statements.statement: For every revealed \(d_n\)-regular graph with \(M_n<n\), the seed design and observed-data Rao--Blackwell estimator are unbiased for \(\tau_n\), and \[Q_G=\sum_{r=1}^{k_n}\binom{k_n}{r}K_G^{\circ r}\succeq0,\qquad \sup_{y\in\mathcal M_n(G)}\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G]\le U(G,k_n).\] Every entry of \(Q_G\), every weight \(w_i(z;G)\), and the certificate are finite graph computations from \(G\) and \(k_n\).
statements.justification: The exact Schur-power identity is the two-arm covariance mechanism that prevents the control estimator from paying the generic conflict spectral radius.
statements.gap: KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, Theorem 4.1, uses randomized priority resolution and a generic conflict-graph norm; UganderYin2023RGCR, Theorem 4.8, studies bounded outcomes within randomized cluster designs. Neither gives this endpoint-\(L_2\) certificate.
statements.consumer: A revealed network can be randomized once and audited before outcomes arrive by evaluating the displayed graph-only certificate.

statements.statement: Using the handle \(\mathsf H_B\), establish \(U(G_n,k_n)\le C_U r(n,d_n)\) with probability tending to one for every admissible degree sequence. One sufficient route is to prove that a universal \(L<\infty\) satisfies \[\Pr\!\left\{\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\right\}\longrightarrow1;\] if that norm statement is false, derive the certificate bound directly from the centered collision expansion without assuming a favorable rate.
statements.justification: This is the sole exposed frontier step: Booleanization, not adjacency spectral control, must save a polynomial factor in the two-arm covariance.
statements.gap: Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Section 2.2, Theorems 14--15, controls polynomial graph matrices, and BauerschmidtEtAl2020EdgeRigidity controls adjacency powers, but Boolean radius-two reachability includes nonlinear collision corrections and the required uniform constant-to-near-square-root degree splice is absent.
statements.consumer: A positive solution certifies the attaining design at the lower-bound rate; a negative solution kills the sampler spine before a false minimax theorem is claimed.

statements.statement: For every finite revealed graph \(G\), an exact branch-safe compiler first evaluates whether \(M_n<n\). If \(M_n\ge n\), it forms none of \(\pi_i(G)\), \(Q_G\), \(w_i(z;G)\), or \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\), and returns the all-treated estimator with worst-case MSE at most \(1=\overline U(G)\). If \(M_n<n\), it enumerates the \(n^{k_n}\) ordered seed tuples, groups them by \(Z^{\mathrm{seed}}\), computes every positive \(\pi_i(G)\), every \(w_i(z;G)\), \(Q_G\), and a certified enclosure of \(\lambda_{\max}(Q_G)\), and returns the seed estimator when \(U(G,k_n)\le1\) or the all-treated fallback otherwise, with worst-case MSE at most \(\overline U(G)\). On the high-probability certificate event in Open-ended Question 1, \(\overline U(G_n)\le C_Ur(n,d_n)\).
statements.justification: The matched statistical frontier comes with an exact finite procedure that never evaluates an inverse exposure probability outside its positive-probability branch.
statements.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Algorithm 4 with Proposition 4.3, gives a polynomial approximation design for its conflict-graph criterion using the imported Partial Vertex Cover 2-approximation in Theorem C.11; it does not provide this branch-safe exact seed-law certificate or close the random-regular GATE minimax gap.
statements.consumer: An experimenter can audit the assignment law and worst-case error on the actual revealed network before running the one-shot study.

statements.statement: There are universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for every admissible degree sequence, \[\Pr\!\left\{c\,r(n,d_n)\le R(G_n)\le C\,r(n,d_n)\right\}\longrightarrow1.\] The upper inequality is attained by the one-shot graph-measurable design-estimator returned by the finite compiler, and the lower inequality ranges over every graph-dependent assignment distribution and measurable estimator. This strictly tightens KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4, from the factor-\(d_n\) interval \(d_n/n\lesssim R(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\) to a matched order, and strictly improves the KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph generic \(d_n^2/n\) GATE upper scale by the factor \(\log(d_n+1)\).
statements.justification: This resolves the full two-arm, all-procedure minimax order rather than optimizing a fixed estimator or exposing only one endpoint arm.
statements.gap: The closest published result is KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4, whose bounds differ by a polynomial factor \(d_n\); the January 2026 one-arm talk is not a full-GATE theorem.
statements.consumer: ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice motivates sizing a larger all-free versus all-fixed random-regular public-goods experiment by the explicit precision cost \(d_n^2/\log(d_n+1)\).

statements.statement: For every finite \(G\), every \(0<\alpha<1\), and every \(y\in\mathcal M_n(G)\), the selected certified procedure satisfies \[\Pr_{\mathcal D_G}\!\left\{\tau_n\in\mathcal C_\alpha(G,Z,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\mid G\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\] On the high-probability event in Theorem 1, its radius is at most \(C^{1/2}d_n/\sqrt{\alpha n\log(d_n+1)}\), which converges to zero throughout the admissible regime.
statements.justification: The risk certificate yields finite-sample design-based coverage under endpoint second moments alone, where Wald conditions and fourth moments are unavailable.
statements.gap: KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph develops Wald intervals under additional moment and dependency restrictions, while HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance optimizes conservative quadratic variance bounds for fixed linear estimators rather than the attained minimax procedure.
statements.consumer: The next random-regular public-goods experiment receives a precomputable honest error bar for the full all-free versus all-fixed policy contrast.

statements.statement: If \(d_n\) is a fixed integer sequence with \(d_n\ge3\), then \(r(n,d_n)=\Theta(n^{-1})\), so Theorem 1 reduces to the ordinary parametric MSE order. If \(G\) has girth at least five, then \(B_2(G)=A_G^2+A_G-(d_n-1)I_n\); hence \(\|A_GP_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(\sqrt{d_n})\) implies \(\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(d_n)\), a strict special case of the open Boolean operator target.
statements.justification: These reductions prevent the proposed frontier from contradicting the no-growth parametric benchmark and isolate Boolean collisions as the only new graph-spectral issue.
statements.gap: BauerschmidtEtAl2020EdgeRigidity and Sarid2023SpectralGap supply adjacency spectral control, but not the Boolean collision identity outside the high-girth special case.
statements.consumer: The fixed degree-four design motivated by ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice recovers order-\(n^{-1}\) MSE and order-\(n^{-1/2}\) confidence radius.

sampling_model.design: The graph \(G=G_n\) is revealed first. The experimenter then chooses a graph-measurable law on \(\{0,1\}^{V_n}\); when \(M_n<n\), the attaining law draws \(k_n\) uniform seeds with replacement and treats the union of their closed neighborhoods, while the finite fallback assigns all units treatment when \(M_n\ge n\).
sampling_model.units: The population \(V_n\) and every potential outcome are fixed conditional on \(G\). The graph is random only for the high-probability frontier statement.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one binary assignment \(Z\) is drawn and all realized outcomes are observed. Seed multiplicities are integrated out of the estimator by conditional Rao--Blackwell weights.
sampling_model.overlap: No unit-level Bernoulli overlap is imposed. The seed branch is entered only when \(M_n<n\), where all endpoint exposure probabilities used in ratios are graph-computable and positive. When \(M_n\ge n\), the compiler forms no inverse-probability quantity and returns the all-treated fallback.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Intermediate-exposure potential outcomes are unrestricted and ignored; no prior outcomes, repeated rounds, endpoint means, behavioral model, or superpopulation outcome law is used.

estimand_functional: \(R(G_n)\asymp r(n,d_n)=d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), attained on the eventual branch \(M_n<n\) by \((\operatorname{Law}(Z^{\mathrm{seed}}\mid G),\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}})\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Corollary 5.4 gives \(d/n\lesssim\mathcal R(G,\tau_{\mathrm{GATE}},2)\lesssim d^2/n\) with high probability for random \(d\)-regular \(G\) and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\).
Theorem 4.1 bounds the modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by \(12.5\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) times the sum of endpoint empirical second moments.
Algorithm 4 is the paper's polynomial approximation design, Proposition 4.3 states its guarantee, and Theorem C.11 is the imported 2-approximation for Partial Vertex Cover used as a subroutine.
Theorem 4.8 bounds GATE Horvitz--Thompson variance for randomized one-hop-max clustering under bounded outcomes and restricted growth.
The paper characterizes admissible estimable quadratic variance bounds and gives convex programs selecting minimally conservative bounds for linear estimators.

tldr: For a revealed uniform simple \(d_n\)-regular network with unrestricted arbitrary neighborhood interference and only endpoint empirical second-moment bounds, the proposed minimax MSE is \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\). A balanced simultaneous-exposure number yields a design-uniform Beta--Bernoulli converse, with its random-regular scale obtained by direct uniform-simple switchings below the verified Kim--Vu threshold and monotone coupling above it. A one-shot with-replacement neighborhood-seed design yields an unbiased observed-data estimator and an exact positive-semidefinite Schur-power covariance certificate on \(M_n<n\); a branch-safe finite compiler returns an all-treated fallback without forming inverse-probability ratios otherwise. The remaining open content is a uniform Boolean radius-two operator estimate, or a direct certificate bound at the same rate; resolving it gives matching bounds over every procedure and an honest shrinking confidence interval for the full GATE.

project_justification.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4, leaves \(d_n/n\lesssim R(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\) for the identical random-regular full-GATE problem, a polynomial factor-\(d_n\) gap. Existing cluster and conflict-graph designs do not supply a matching all-procedure converse or exploit balanced two-arm endpoint revelation.
project_justification.niche: The bipartite GATE conflict geometry singles out two unstudied objects: the largest balanced pair of opposite endpoint centers at distance greater than two and the centered covariance of control exposure under a fixed-count neighborhood-seed assignment.
project_justification.fill: The proposal characterizes the balanced-packing scale using direct uniform-simple switchings below the verified sandwich threshold and monotone coupling above it, converts that scale to an all-design Bayes lower bound, and matches it with a graph-measurable seed design whose covariance has an exact Schur-power representation. A branch-safe finite compiler avoids undefined exposure ratios, and a centered Boolean collision theorem closes the only remaining upper-bound step before the graph certificate yields finite-sample coverage.

related_work: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, arXiv:2608.04909v1, Corollary 5.4 and Appendix E.4, is the closest comparator: it places the identical random-regular GATE risk between \(d_n/n\) and \(d_n^2/n\), while Sections 3.2--3.3 build design-based Le Cam mixtures from one-sided conflict-graph information. Its Algorithm 4 and Proposition 4.3 give its polynomial approximation design, using the imported Partial Vertex Cover 2-approximation in Theorem C.11; the exact branch-safe seed compiler is informed by that algorithm but certifies a different assignment law. KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, arXiv:2411.10908v3, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1, supplies randomized priority conflict resolution and the \(\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) covariance-norm upper bound; the proposed seed law replaces that generic geometry and strictly improves its random-regular GATE scale. UganderYin2023RGCR, Sections 2.3 and 4.3, randomizes graph decompositions and integrates exposure probabilities, but Theorem 4.8 assumes uniformly bounded outcomes and evaluates a fixed Horvitz--Thompson procedure rather than unrestricted minimax risk. AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference supplies the exposure-mapping and inverse-probability foundation. CooperEtAl2002RandomRegular studies ordinary independence rather than signed balanced radius-two packing. BehagueIlkovicMontgomery2025Sandwich, Theorem 1.1, supplies the monotone transfer only in its verified regime \(d_n\ge C\log n\); the below-threshold argument is instead a direct degree-preserving switching enumeration under the uniform simple law. Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Section 2.2, Theorems 14--15, motivates graph-shape trace moments for polynomial matrices, while BauerschmidtEtAl2020EdgeRigidity and Sarid2023SpectralGap control nonconstant adjacency eigenvalues; none covers Boolean collision corrections uniformly over the target regime. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance, Sections 4--6, explains why variance is generally unestimable and how conservative quadratic bounds can be optimized, but it does not select the minimax design. ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice provides the prospective consumer: its first-round all-free versus all-fixed degree-four public-goods comparison is local to closed pools and was run with only two whole-network replicates per setup.
technical_internal_limitation: The stronger heuristic \(\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(d_n)\) is not needed and is not claimed. A row-sum bound on duplicate walks is inadequate near \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) because it retains a large approximately constant component. Exact finite enumeration and observed spectra are falsification checks only and cannot establish the uniform asymptotic operator statement.
honest_scope: The balanced Bayes calculation, the direct uniform-simple switching argument below the verified sandwich threshold, the monotone coupling above it, and the Schur covariance identity are presolve evidence to be independently proved, not established inputs. Open-ended Question 1 is load-bearing; the matched theorem is not asserted independently of it. The seed probabilities, covariance matrix, Rao--Blackwell weights, and seed estimator are defined only when \(M_n<n\); on the complementary finite branch the compiler returns the all-treated fallback without forming any ratio. The proposal concerns one assignment, unrestricted intermediate ANI outcomes, and the full population GATE. It does not cover later strategic feedback, final wealth, two-hop individual payoff, repeated experiments, nonuniform graph draws, or claims that the ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice behavioral model is worst case. As sanity checks, fixed degree gives the standard \(n^{-1}\) MSE order, and high-girth expanders reduce the Boolean operator to an adjacency polynomial.

seed_details.anchor_location: Corollary 5.4, Sections 3.2--3.3, Appendix E.4, and Section 7
seed_details.kernel: Prove the uniform high-probability matched frontier \(R(G_n)\asymp d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) with a one-shot attaining design-estimator and an all-procedure converse.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the anchor's one-sided induced-independence lower statistic by balanced two-arm exposure and replace its generic conflict-spectral upper design by fixed-count neighborhood seeds.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for random-regular GATE minimax risk, simultaneous treated-control exposure, and the displayed logarithmic rate found no closer public theorem beyond the anchor's factor-\(d_n\) interval.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from Corollary 5.4 because the random-regular graph square has degree \(d_n^2\). Rebuttal: that corollary explicitly leaves \(d_n/n\) versus \(d_n^2/n\), and graph-square degree does not measure balanced two-arm information or the proposed centered covariance.

seed_details.kernel: Characterize \(\beta(G_n)=\Theta_{\Pr}(n\log(d_n+1)/d_n^2)\) and derive a finite-population Bayes lower bound against every design and estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: At the anchor's exposure-reveal reduction, retain the smaller of the treated and control endpoint counts rather than the total independent set size.
seed_details.destination_search: CooperEtAl2002RandomRegular occupies ordinary independence, but searches found no signed distance-two balanced-packing theorem or Bayes-to-GATE conversion.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: ordinary random-regular independence asymptotics already imply the claim. Rebuttal: ordinary independence forbids conflicts within one color, whereas the GATE conflict graph has edges only across opposite colors and requires balanced information in both arms.

seed_details.anchor_location: Algorithm 1, Theorem 4.1, proof in Appendix D.4, and Section 7
seed_details.kernel: Construct a two-arm seed design with an exact positive-semidefinite Schur covariance and prove a uniform Boolean radius-two operator certificate at the lower-bound rate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace priority conflict resolution and entrywise absolute covariance bounds by a fixed-count seed law whose negative dependence subtracts the constant radius-two overlap component.
seed_details.destination_search: Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices treats polynomial graph matrices and adjacency papers treat walk counts; searches found no theorem for the centered Boolean radius-two incidence matrix in the full degree range.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: adjacency spectral rigidity immediately controls graph powers. Rebuttal: Boolean reachability thresholds repeated paths and triangles, so \(B_2(G)\) is not \(A_G^2\) outside high girth and the collision correction is load-bearing.

seed_details.anchor_location: Section 4, Algorithm 4 and Proposition 4.3; Appendix C.3, Theorem C.11; and Section 7
seed_details.kernel: Give a polynomial-time graph algorithm with an observable certificate within a constant of \(R(G_n)\) on typical random-regular inputs.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Algorithm 4's approximation of the conflict-graph criterion, whose Proposition 4.3 guarantee uses the imported Partial Vertex Cover subroutine in Theorem C.11, by compilation of the seed law and a certificate directly comparable with the balanced lower statistic.
seed_details.destination_search: Viviano et al. optimize within cluster designs, while the anchor's Algorithm 4 and Proposition 4.3 approximate its conflict-graph criterion; no located result gives a constant-factor certificate for unrestricted random-regular GATE risk.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: Algorithm 4 with Proposition 4.3 already supplies the algorithm. Rebuttal: that result approximates the paper's conflict-graph criterion using Theorem C.11 only as an imported Partial Vertex Cover subroutine; it does not certify the true minimax risk, and a constant comparison to \(R(G_n)\) is precisely missing.
seed_details.decision: drop: the finite compiler is retained in the chosen kernel, but polynomial running time would add an unverified complexity bottleneck.

seed_details.kernel: Characterize the shortest honest one-shot confidence radius under only the endpoint empirical-\(L_2\) ellipsoid and the attained design.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the Wald normal approximation by inversion of a graph-only worst-case risk certificate, then test whether the \(\alpha^{-1/2}\) dependence is minimax necessary.
seed_details.destination_search: HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance studies estimable quadratic variance bounds, but no located source gives confidence-radius optimality under this endpoint ellipsoid and jointly optimized design.

literature_map.settled: The conflict graph determines the decision problem abstractly; Corollary 5.4 proves only \(d_n/n\lesssim R(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\) for the target regime.
literature_map.open: Neither the balanced two-arm reveal statistic nor a matching random-regular full-GATE procedure is characterized.

literature_map.settled: Conflict resolution and randomized clustering give computable exposure probabilities and fixed-procedure variance bounds.
literature_map.open: Their random-regular bounds do not match an all-procedure converse under signed endpoint empirical-\(L_2\) outcomes.

literature_map.settled: Ordinary independence has logarithmic scale, and binomial graphs can be coupled below random regular graphs above logarithmic degree.
literature_map.open: Signed balanced closed-neighborhood packing uniformly from constant degree to \(o(\sqrt n)\) is not covered.

literature_map.settled: Polynomial graph matrices and nonconstant adjacency eigenvalues admit sharp switching, trace, or local-law control in overlapping degree regimes.
literature_map.open: The centered Boolean radius-two matrix has nonlinear duplicate-walk corrections and no located uniform theorem at the required scale.

literature_map.settled: Variance is generally not estimable under interference, while conservative quadratic bounds and Wald results are available under additional structure.
literature_map.open: The attained minimax procedure needs an honest finite-sample interval under endpoint second moments alone.

novelty_justification.closest_results: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4, leaves the exact factor-d interval in the identical model; KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, Theorem 4.1, gives the strongest generic implementable upper construction.
novelty_justification.exact_delta: The proposed theorem replaces that interval by the closed-form order d squared divided by n log(d+1), ranges over every design and measurable estimator, and attains the order with one graph-measurable assignment and observed-data estimator.
novelty_justification.non_subsumption: Ordinary independence does not balance GATE arms; adjacency spectra do not control Boolean collision corrections; cluster-design bounds do not optimize over all procedures.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic:
The simultaneous-exposure frontier for global treatment effects on random regular networks. For every admissible integer sequence n→∞, 3≤d_n=o(sqrt(n)), nd_n even, draw G_n uniformly from labeled simple d_n-regular graphs and reveal it to the experimenter. Conditional on G=G_n, potential outcomes y_i(z) are arbitrary real functions of z restricted to the closed neighborhood N_G[i], obeying n^-1 sum_i y_i(1)^2≤1 and n^-1 sum_i y_i(0)^2≤1; other exposures are unrestricted. Choose any distribution D on {0,1}^n, then observe one draw Z and all y_i(Z). The target is τ=n^-1 sum_i[y_i(1)-y_i(0)]. Define R(G)=inf_(D,measurable estimator) sup_y E_D[(τhat-τ)^2]. Both D and estimator can depend on G; no endpoint means are known and no prior outcomes, repeat rounds, or model restrictions beyond ANI are supplied. Determine an closed-form deterministic rate r(n,d), not defined as the original minimax optimization, and construct design-estimator pairs such that, for every admissible degree sequence, with probability 1-o(1) over G_n, c r(n,d_n) ≤ R(G_n) ≤ C r(n,d_n), with universal positive constants. Deliver matching bounds including any essential logarithmic or transition factors, and a finite graph computation route producing the attaining design or certified approximation at the same rate. The answer r is open: do not assume d/n or d²/n. Inferential corollary: derive a computable nonvacuous design-based error/CI guarantee from the attained risk, retaining the full population GATE. The result must close the polynomial factor-d gap for diverging degrees; merely restating the original upper/lower interval is failure. FIELD CONTRACT: Resolve the full two-arm global-effect minimax order in the random-regular regime, with an attaining one-shot design-estimator and matching lower bound over every procedure. A one-arm HT bound, fixed-estimator variance optimum, worst-graph construction, logarithmic tweak alone, or repeated experiments is out of scope. PRIOR ART: Distinct from active exp_mixed_design_degree_frontier: its affine known-weight outcome model and mixed-estimator worst-graph d² construction do not solve unrestricted ANI random-regular risk. Distinct from banked exp_bipartite_minimax_design and queued AWRI finite-rule exact risk/spatial FPT/quadratic interference specification test. Full-GATE conflict graph lower/upper gap remains explicit in August2026 anchor; do not claim that the Jan2026 talk already solved it. CONSUMER: Shi et al. (2020), Freedom of choice adds value to public goods, PNAS117:17516–17521, doi10.1073/pnas.1921806117, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7395457/ . Their random-regular degree4 arm directly compares the policy in which everyone may freely allocate contributions with the policy in which everyone has fixed allocation; first-round participation and public-good provision are measured before feedback. They use two whole-network replicates per setup. The concrete consumer is sizing and randomizing this same all-free-versus-all-fixed provision comparison: whether a mixed assignment in a larger random-regular network can estimate the full-policy effect with a shrinking robust error, and how its precision depends on network degree. For a one-round local-pool outcome, only that pool’s members’ contribution decisions enter; all later-round strategic feedback, final wealth, and two-hop individual total payoff are outside this theorem. The theorem gives a robust ANI benchmark, not a claim that their exact behavioral model attains worst-case risk or that their finite networks were uniform graph draws. It may change the next experiment’s allocation between network size, degree and whole-network replication; it does not reinterpret their existing multi-round findings. This published policy comparison supplies the applied question, while the new design is the theorem’s prospective use.
PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The draft derives a finite-population Beta–Bernoulli lower bound using the maximum balanced pair of simultaneously exposed endpoint sets. A configuration-model argument for small degrees and a verified binomial-to-regular coupling for larger degrees support a lower rate d²/[n log(d+1)]. A single assignment generated by independent seed draws with replacement gives unbiased estimates of both endpoint means. The control covariance has an exact positive-semidefinite Schur-power expansion, producing a graph-computable risk certificate under the original endpoint L2 bounds. Conditioning seed multiplicities on the assignment removes hidden randomization metadata. Exact enumeration checks joint probabilities, signed and spiked outcomes, and this conditioning step. The full matched theorem remains unproved.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a uniform high-probability bound ||B₂(I−11ᵀ/n)||=O(d^(7/4)) for the Boolean radius-two incidence matrix throughout 3≤d=o(√n), or directly establish the same-rate covariance certificate. Expand and independently audit the lower-bound constants and external graph-theorem applications.
EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the exact identities and test the Boolean matrix and actual certificate across all degree ranges, including near √n. A proved typical excess over the proposed rate kills this sampler spine; failure of the stronger O(d) conjecture alone does not.
